To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) binge eating is a complex phenomenon and its occurrence is connected with many factors, such as genetic predisposition and environmental factors; (2) binge eating is associated with a number of diseases, including obesity, depression and anxiety; (3) animal models of bingeing can be used to study neurobiological mechanisms underlying this disorder; (4) new, centrally acting anti obesity drugs can be used in the treatment of binge eating disorder.
binge eating in pre clinical animal models is a result of disturbed functioning of the central reward system, and that the drugs acting on this system can be a new promising treatment for obesity.

the most important neurobiological mechanisms underlying binge eating in animal models include the hypothalamic-pituitary adrenal axis and the hypothalamic neuropeptides such as orexin, neuropeptide Y and agouti-related peptide, which are involved in regulation of appetite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new, effective anti-obesity drug, with no side effects and a high safety profile.
the development of novel antiobesity drugs with the use of animal models of bingeing and related neurobiological studies.
the development of a new, safe and effective pharmacological treatment for the binge eating disease.

binge eating in preclinical models is a phenomenon, which can be successfully used to model binge eating in humans.
binge eating is a complex behavior that involves multiple brain regions, which are involved in reward processing and motivation.
